slot.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slot.brief: Light/EM wave of given intensity or power falls on a surface (reflecting/absorbing, possibly at angle); compute radiation pressure and force on the surface.

stem: A beam of power $9$ W strikes a stationary surface at $60^\circ$ to its normal. One-third of the incident power is reflected specularly and the rest is absorbed. Taking $c=3.0\times10^8$ m s$^{-1}$, find the magnitude of the force on the surface.

verdicts.working: Incident momentum rate is (9/c)(sin60°, cos60°); reflected momentum rate is (3/c)(sin60°, −cos60°). Their difference gives force components (√3, 2)×10⁻⁸ N, so the magnitude is √7×10⁻⁸ N.

working:
Let $r=1/3$. $F_n=(1+r)P\cos60^\circ/c=2.0\times10^{-8}$ N; $F_t=(1-r)P\sin60^\circ/c=\sqrt{3}\times10^{-8}$ N. $F=\sqrt{F_n^2+F_t^2}=\sqrt{7}\times10^{-8}$ N.

Independent check: Incident momentum rate is (9/c)(sin60°, cos60°); reflected momentum rate is (3/c)(sin60°, −cos60°). Their difference gives force components (√3, 2)×10⁻⁸ N, so the magnitude is √7×10⁻⁸ N.
solution:
For reflected fraction $r=1/3$, the normal and tangential force components are
$$F_n=\frac{(1+r)P\cos60^\circ}{c}=2.0\times10^{-8}\,\text{N},\qquad F_t=\frac{(1-r)P\sin60^\circ}{c}=\sqrt{3}\times10^{-8}\,\text{N}.$$
Hence $F=\sqrt{F_n^2+F_t^2}=\sqrt{7}\times10^{-8}\,\text{N}$.
